Thirty-eight comments

Learned from the playing of Jesse Smith on a Cherish the Ladies album. They list it simply as “B minor Reel” *grr* If you need to practice your b rolls this is the tune to play! :)

-Jonathan

↳ Posted by jdave on June 13th, 2004.

The Flooded Road To Glenties

Reel written by Jimmy McHugh, posted on behalf of bb as it is one of her favourite tunes. Transcribed from Liz Doherty’s album “Quare Imagination”. In practice her long rolls start on the note below, followed by a short roll, but I’ve simplified this for the transcription, so for example e~f2e I’ve written as ~f3e and A~B2A as ~B3A.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on August 25th, 2004.

Ideas for some chords

|:Bm A |A E|Bm A|C#m F#m|
F#m A|G D|F#m|A E:|
|:Bm|Bm A|Bm A|C#m F#m|
F#m A|G D|F#m|A E:|

↳ Posted by ithaca-markb on February 8th, 2024.

Re: The Flooded Road To Glenties

Coincidentally, I’ve just been listening to this tune - probably Jimmy’s “Greatest Hit” - recorded by Paul Bradley.
Worth quoting from his sleeve notes, methinks :
"I heard it from Jimmy McHugh who composed it. He was playing in a quiet back-room of the Highlands Hotel in Glenties. Inspirationfor the tune came, he told me, when a car he was a passenger inbroke down in a bad flood.
“Well”, he said, “ we can either sit here and play a tune , or we can get out and push. There’ll have to be a tune writ about it”.
My second meeting with Jimmy was at a festival in Turinat which we were both playing. A small audience which I joined was enjoying Jimmy’s meek and marvellous music in a shady off-stage nook. When I leaned over to him and said “Give us ”The Flooded Road To Glenties“, he was so surprised ( if not shocked ) at the global circulation of his tune and our chance meeting, that it took little convincing for him to write outthe tune for me. Ten years later it hasn’t lost it’s appeal”.
A small insight into the traditional Irish music legend that was Jimmy McHugh [ RIP ].

Re: The Flooded Road To Glenties

Hi Ben,
Yes, it was after playing through Enda’s lesson that I wanted to cement
the tune in my head by listening to some other versions (Enda’s brother Fergal
has it on one of his tune-a-day videos from 2017). I like Hannah’s take on the tune.
I got to play on “stage” with Hannah and Evan Powell (piano) one lunchtime at
the O’Flaherty Retreat in Texas last October.

Even though I started learning the tune on tenor banjo, I find that it suits
the C#/D box better -- at least it’s easier to play as fast as Hannah plays it on the box.

The Flooded Road To Glenties, X:14

A few tweaks to make this sit on flute / whistle.
You can swap in a little rest to replace the 8th note in a few places, to set up some of the difficult bars.
Also the f# replacing a d in the B part second bar is a help.

I first heard this monster little tune from fiddler James McNamara.

Love out
Pat
